name: Brute-force followed by authentication from the same IP
description: Detects an SSH brute-force alert followed by successful authentication on the same Wazuh agent within 15 minutes.
limitations: Same agent and source IP do not prove account compromise or matching usernames: failures use data.srcuser and successes data.dstuser. An unrelated success from another IP cannot complete the sequence.
deployment_prerequisites: Collect SSH brute-force and successful authentication alerts with populated native source IP and agent join fields.
historical_scope: Earlier versions only; not final-expression validation
offline_validation: Repository structure and source preservation only

name: SSH followed by sensitive sudo activity
description: Detects successful SSH authentication followed by privileged command execution within 15 minutes.
limitations: SSH and sudo users are not equated. Substring matching can miss shells and alternative commands. This contextual rule overlaps PRIV-001 and PERS-001; prefer their additional evidence. Routine administration can match.
deployment_prerequisites: Collect SSH and sudo alerts with native command and target-user fields; review sensitive-command coverage.
historical_scope: Earlier versions only; not final-expression validation
offline_validation: Repository structure and source preservation only

name: SSH followed by realtime sensitive file modification
description: Correlates remote access with subsequent modification of sensitive Linux authentication or access-control files. This SSH-linked rule is restricted to realtime FIM events
limitations: Realtime FIM reduces timing ambiguity but does not identify a process or SSH session. Scheduled-only monitoring is excluded and must remain covered by separate FIM alerts.
deployment_prerequisites: Enable realtime FIM for the specified authentication, sudoers and authorised-key paths.
historical_scope: Earlier versions only; not final-expression validation
offline_validation: Repository structure and source preservation only

name: SSH login, sudo and sensitive file modification
description: Detects a three-stage sequence involving remote access, privilege use and modification of security-sensitive files.
limitations: Agent and time correlation does not prove actor or session continuity. Unlike SSH-003 this source has no realtime FIM predicate; scheduled observation timing can misattribute changes. Legitimate administration can match.
deployment_prerequisites: Collect SSH, sudo and sensitive-path FIM alerts; assess scheduled FIM observation delays.
historical_scope: Earlier versions only; not final-expression validation
offline_validation: Repository structure and source preservation only

name: SSH login, SCP execution and file modification
description: Detects an SSH login followed by SCP execution and a file creation or modification event.
limitations: SCP command telemetry and FIM are joined only by agent and time; no transferred-file, user or session equality is enforced. Scheduled FIM and legitimate transfers can match.
deployment_prerequisites: Collect rule 92603 audit command telemetry identifying scp, SSH authentication and file FIM alerts.
historical_scope: Earlier versions only; not final-expression validation
offline_validation: Repository structure and source preservation only

name: Web reconnaissance followed by exploitation attempt
description: This rule correlates reconnaissance and exploitation indicators originating from the same recorded HTTP client IP against the same Wazuh-monitored endpoint.
limitations: Same recorded client IP does not confirm exploitation. Historical attribution is uncertain because the recorded client address also represented the server public address; reverse proxies can link unrelated activity.
deployment_prerequisites: Collect HTTP reconnaissance and exploitation alerts; validate recorded client IP attribution through proxies.
historical_scope: Earlier versions only; not final-expression validation
offline_validation: Repository structure and source preservation only

name: Web attack followed by suspicious PHP file creation
description: This rule detects web attack indicators followed by the creation of a PHP file in the WordPress uploads directory.
limitations: PHP creation is joined by endpoint and time, not HTTP client identity; causality is unproven. Legitimate deployments can create PHP files.
deployment_prerequisites: Collect web alerts and added-file FIM in the exact WordPress Docker volume path; verify that path locally.
historical_scope: Earlier versions only; not final-expression validation
offline_validation: Repository structure and source preservation only

name: Server-side exploitation indicator followed by PHP file creation
description: This rule uses a narrower selection of web exploitation indicators followed by PHP file creation.
limitations: Investigative correlation only: HTTP 200 does not prove exploitation. FIM detection time may differ from creation time, and legitimate deployments may match.
deployment_prerequisites: Collect the narrower exploitation rule IDs and added-file FIM at the exact WordPress Docker volume path.
historical_scope: Earlier versions only; not final-expression validation
offline_validation: Repository structure and source preservation only

name: PHP file creation followed by HTTP access attempt
description: This is the revised version. Instead of accepting general suspicious web activity after PHP creation, it requires a subsequent HTTP request targeting a PHP URL within the WordPress uploads directory.
limitations: The requested PHP URL is not verified against the exact created file. Nested upload paths are included; the request stage deliberately has no rule-ID restriction, allowing other classifications including 31101.
deployment_prerequisites: Collect added-file FIM at the exact WordPress Docker volume path and native URL telemetry for uploads requests.
historical_scope: Earlier versions only; not final-expression validation
offline_validation: Repository structure and source preservation only

name: SSH access → privileged account creation
description: Detects a successful SSH login followed by sudo activity targeting root and a subsequent new-user event on the same monitored endpoint.
limitations: The source says the optional third-stage key accommodates missing data.srcuser and that account creation remains associated by agent and time. Optional-field syntax does not itself guarantee wildcard joining: missing values can become null and fail to join a non-null username. Verify this claim in the target engine; do not silently change the query. SSH-to-sudo attribution is stronger, but account creation causality remains unproven. sudo su followed by useradd in a root shell is intentionally excluded.
deployment_prerequisites: Collect SSH destination usernames, sudo source usernames and commands, and 5902 new-user events. Validate stage-specific joins and missing third-stage usernames explicitly.
historical_scope: Earlier versions only; not final-expression validation
offline_validation: Repository structure and source preservation only

name: SSH login → crontab editor → cron modification
description: Detects an SSH login followed by a crontab editor event and a FIM alert for a cron-related file.
limitations: Legitimate cron administration can produce the same sequence; agent and time do not establish actor continuity.
deployment_prerequisites: Collect SSH, 2834 crontab-editor alerts and FIM for all specified cron paths.
historical_scope: Earlier versions only; not final-expression validation
offline_validation: Repository structure and source preservation only

name: SSH login → systemd unit modification → service failure
description: Detects an SSH login followed by modification or creation of a systemd service unit and a subsequent service-failure alert.
limitations: A service failure after a unit-file change does not establish causality. Legitimate service installation and maintenance can match.
deployment_prerequisites: Collect SSH, systemd unit-file FIM and 40704 service-failure alerts.
historical_scope: Earlier versions only; not final-expression validation
offline_validation: Repository structure and source preservation only

name: sudo → audit configuration change → audit daemon stopped
description: Detects sudo activity followed by an audit configuration change and an audit daemon stop event.
limitations: Legitimate audit-service maintenance can match this potentially significant defence-evasion sequence.
deployment_prerequisites: Collect sudo plus audit CONFIG_CHANGE and daemon-stop alerts; ensure audit telemetry is available.
historical_scope: Earlier versions only; not final-expression validation
offline_validation: Repository structure and source preservation only

name: System executable modification → rootcheck anomaly
description: The revision prioritises more recent FIM observations, excludes the recurring /dev/null\r finding and requires a rootcheck anomaly that concerns the same executable path.
limitations: Requires rootcheck to expose the same executable path in data.file.keyword; population outside the recurring anomaly is unestablished. Realtime-only FIM excludes scheduled observations and reduces coverage. Matching paths and timing do not establish malware execution.
deployment_prerequisites: Enable realtime FIM for executable paths and establish rootcheck data.file.keyword population and exact path formatting, including carriage-return handling.
historical_scope: Earlier versions only; not final-expression validation
offline_validation: Repository structure and source preservation only
